# How the repository is organized

This repository holds the robot's sources and the record side by side. The sources are upstream's, kept as
published; the record is what the fork adds around them.

![Repository map: the robot's sources (mechanical, electrical, simulation model) classed by the safety-relevant file list, the assurance record folder by folder, and everything generated from it, with CI checking every one on every pull request.](../docs/assets/asimov/repo-map.svg)

*Generated by [`make_assets.py`](../docs/assets/asimov/make_assets.py). Left: the robot's sources, classed by the
safety-relevant file list. Middle: the record. Right: what is generated from it and never edited by hand.*

## The robot's sources

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`mechanical/`](../mechanical/) | The CAD of the seven subassemblies, pelvis to head, as STEP files grouped by fabrication method (machined 7075 aluminium, MJF PA12 nylon, SLM 316L stainless, off-the-shelf) |
| [`electrical/`](../electrical/README.md) | The motion control board (a Radxa CM5 carrier with six CAN ports, KiCad sources and device tree) and the actuator power and CAN harness |
| [`sim-model/`](../sim-model/README.md) | The MuJoCo model the locomotion policy is trained with: masses, joint ranges, control ranges |

Changed only through the fork's change process, never silently; the assessed upstream commit is named in the
[gap assessment](../assurance/00-assessment/gap-assessment.md) header and in baseline BL-001. The firmware, the
Asimov API and the locomotion policy are not in any public repository and get safety-relevant path patterns when
they are pinned ([WP-M-10](../assurance/01-management/WP-M-10-upstream-and-supplier-management.md)). Upstream's
manual and roadmap are quoted, never restated.

## The record

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`assurance/`](../assurance/README.md) | Every work product, analysis, decision and review |
| [`assurance/00-assessment/concept-package/`](../assurance/00-assessment/concept-package/README.md) | The fork's earlier concept-phase package, kept unedited as the record's seed |
| [`assurance/process/`](../assurance/process/README.md) | The integrated process model: activities, lanes, interfaces and gates as data; generated process maps |
| [`assurance/case/`](../assurance/case/README.md) | The Living Safety Case records, their validator and the dashboard generator |
| [`assurance/01-management/decisions/`](../assurance/01-management/decisions/README.md) | The decision register and the inbox page builder |
| [`assurance/tools/`](../assurance/tools/) | The folder index generator, the link and table checkers |
| [`docs/`](../docs/README.md) | The architecture overview and the generated README figures |
| [`tools/wiki/`](../tools/wiki/) | The wiki build tool and infographics |
| [`wiki/`](../wiki/README.md) | These pages |
| [`.github/workflows/`](../.github/workflows) | The assurance checks and the wiki sync |

Changed by pull request to `main` and checked by the workflows below.

## The assurance tree, folder by folder

Folders are numbered in lifecycle order. Each work product is named `WP`, a letter for its area, and a number; the
[glossary](Glossary.md) decodes the letters. The authoritative table, with the standard clauses each folder answers
to, is in [`assurance/README.md`](../assurance/README.md#layout), and each folder's README is generated from the
register.

| Folder | Prefix | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `00-assessment/` | | Gap assessment of the inherited repository and the concept-phase package, GAP-01…GAP-34; the package itself |
| `01-management/` | `WP-M` | Assurance strategy, safety plan, confirmation measures, regulatory strategy, cybersecurity and ML plans, upstream management, impact analysis, the decision register |
| `02-concept/` | `WP-C` | Item definition and limits, operating envelopes, risk assessment, safety functions and required PL, risk reduction concept, interaction, contact limits and misuse, cybersecurity and ML concepts, insufficiency analysis of perception and the policy |
| `03-system/` | `WP-S` | Safety requirements specification, stop-chain and safety-layer architecture, fall-arrest and response-time budget, safety-chain I/O, installation and tether requirements, cybersecurity architecture, system verification |
| `04-hardware/` | `WP-H` | Stop-chain hardware, electrical and battery safety, failure analysis, PL calculation, component qualification, structural and stability analysis |
| `05-software/` | `WP-W` | The safety layer on the motion control board: environment, requirements, architecture, safety analysis, units, verification, safety parameters, ML engineering of the policy |
| `06-validation/` | `WP-V` | Safety validation, stability and fall tests, contact and detection validation, E-stop validation, fault injection, cybersecurity validation, the test operations hold point, field trials |
| `07-supporting/` | `WP-P` | Configuration, change, problem resolution, documentation, review, traceability, tool and component qualification, release |
| `08-analyses/` | `WP-A` | FMEA, FTA, common cause failure, STPA, independence of the chain from the policy and the tele-operation stack |
| `09-production-operation/` | `WP-O` | Kit assembly and commissioning, operation, information for use, field monitoring, incident response |
| `10-safety-case/` | `WP-K` | The safety case, the technical documentation index, the cybersecurity case, assessment reports, release record, AI Act record; gate and confirmation records |
| `process/`, `trace/`, `case/` | `WP-P-11`, `WP-T-01` | The process model with its maps and swimlane figures, the trace items (hazards, safety functions, assumptions of use) and the Living Safety Case records with their validator and dashboard |

## What checks a change

Every workflow lives in [`.github/workflows/`](../.github/workflows).

| Workflow | Runs when | What it checks |
|---|---|---|
| [assurance](../.github/workflows/assurance.yaml) | Every pull request and push to `main` | The Living Safety Case records, their validator tests and the dashboard; the decision register's lifecycle rules and its figure; the folder indexes against the register; the process model with its maps, gate skeletons and swimlane figures; the README figures against their generator; relative links; Markdown tables |
| [wiki](../.github/workflows/wiki.yaml) | Every pull request, and every push to `main` | Builds these pages and checks that every link target still exists; on a push, syncs them and the rendered infographics to the GitHub wiki |

A passing workflow accepts nothing on its own. It can be evidence that a reviewer accepts; see
[contributing](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

## What is generated

| Generated | From | By |
|---|---|---|
| Folder READMEs under `assurance/` | WP-M-00 §3 | `assurance/tools/folder_index.py` |
| Process maps and gate skeletons | `assurance/process/model/`, WP-M-00, WP-M-02, WP-M-06 | `assurance/process/tools/process_model.py` |
| Process swimlanes, lifecycle grid and interface figures | The same model | `assurance/process/tools/process_figures.py` |
| Living Safety Case dashboard, status, badge and README blocks | `assurance/case/` records | `assurance/case/tools/generate_dashboard.py` |
| README and wiki figures (hero, standards, architecture, roadmap, lifecycle, status card, standards map, repository map) | The data in the generator and the records | `docs/assets/asimov/make_assets.py` |
| Decision lifecycle figure | The decisions README | `assurance/01-management/decisions/fig_lifecycle.py` |
| The decision inbox page | `register.yaml` | `assurance/01-management/decisions/build_inbox.py` |
| Wiki infographics | `register.yaml`, WP-M-00, the safety-relevant file list, the workflows | `tools/wiki/infographics.py` at sync |

None of them is edited by hand; CI fails when one is stale.
